'''Andrew Jay Feustel''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|f|oɪ|s|t|əl}}; born August 25, 1965) is an American/Canadian former [[NASA]] [[astronaut]] and [[geophysicist]]. Following several years working as a geophysicist, Feustel was selected as an astronaut candidate by NASA in July 2000. He is the veteran of 3 space flights with NASA.<ref name=NASAbio/> His first [[spaceflight]] in May 2009, [[STS-125]], lasted just under 13 days.<ref name="nasabio">{{cite web |url=https://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/biographies/andrew-j-feustel/biography |title=Andrew J. Feustel |last=Whiting |first=Melanie |date=October 5, 2018 |publisher=NASA |access-date=October 24, 2018
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101142427/https://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/biographies/andrew-j-feustel/biography
|archive-date=November 1, 2018}}</ref><ref name="SR1">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/shuttlemissions/sts125/news/STS-125-01.html |title=STS-125 MCC Status Report #01 |access-date=May 11, 2009 |publisher=NASA |date=May 11, 2009 |author=NASA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090515122725/http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/shuttlemissions/sts125/news/STS-125-01.html |archive-date=May 15, 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref> This mission was the fifth and final mission to service the [[Hubble Space Telescope]], aboard [[Space Shuttle]] [[Space Shuttle Atlantis|''Atlantis'']]. Feustel performed three [[Extra-vehicular activity|spacewalks]] during the mission.<ref name=EA-bio>{{cite web |url=http://www.astronautix.com/astros/feustel.htm |title=Feustel |publisher=[[Encyclopedia Astronautica]] |access-date=December 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101129080610/http://astronautix.com/astros/feustel.htm |archive-date=November 29, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His second spaceflight was [[STS-134]], which launched on May 16, 2011 to deliver the [[Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer]] to the [[International Space Station]] (ISS) and was the final flight of {{OV|105}} and was the penultimate flight of the [[Space Shuttle program]]. Feustel returned to the ISS on March 21, 2018 aboard [[Soyuz MS-08]], to serve as a member of [[Expedition 55]] and was the ISS Commander during [[Expedition 56]]. After returning to Earth, he became the Deputy [[Chief of the Astronaut Office|Chief of the NASA Astronaut Office]] in 2020, and served as acting Chief Astronaut starting in November 2022. Feustel retired from NASA in July 2023.

==Education and early career==
Feustel was born in [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="nasabio" /><ref name="interview">{{cite web |access-date=September 21, 2008 |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/shuttlemissions/hst_sm4/interview_Feustel.html |author=NASA |title=Preflight Interview: Andrew Feustel, Mission Specialist |date=July 31, 2008 |publisher=NASA9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080925045706/http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/shuttlemissions/hst_sm4/interview_Feustel.html |archive-date=September 25, 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> He grew up in [[Lake Orion, Michigan]], where he graduated from [[Lake Orion High School]] in 1983, and received an [[Associate's degree|Associate of Science]] degree from [[Oakland Community College]] in 1985. He then attended [[Purdue University]], where he was a member of [[Sigma Phi Epsilon]] fraternity and received both a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in solid earth sciences in 1989 and a [[Master of Science]] degree in geophysics in 1991. He then moved to [[Ontario]], Canada to attend [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], where he received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[Earth science|geological science]]s in 1995.<ref name="nasabio" />

While attending community college, Feustel worked as an auto mechanic at International Autoworks, Ltd., [[Farmington Hills, Michigan]], restoring 1950s [[Jaguar Cars|Jaguars]].<ref name="nasabio" /> At Purdue University, Feustel served as a Residence Hall Counselor for two years at Cary Quadrangle for the Purdue University Student Housing organization. His summers were spent working as a commercial and industrial [[glazier]] near his home in Michigan. During his master's degree studies Feustel worked as a Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant in the Earth and Atmospheric Sciences Department of Purdue University. His M.S. thesis investigated physical property measurements of rock specimens under elevated hydrostatic pressures simulating Earth's deep crustal environments. While at Purdue, Feustel served for three years as [[Purdue Grand Prix|Grand Prix]] Chairman and team Kart driver for Sigma Phi Epsilon Fraternity.<ref name="nasabio" /> In 1991, Feustel moved to [[Kingston, Ontario]], Canada to attend Queen's University where he worked as a Graduate Research Assistant and Graduate Teaching Assistant. Feustel's Ph.D. thesis investigated [[Attenuation#Earthquake|seismic wave attenuation]] in underground mines and measurement techniques and applications to site characterization.<ref name="nasabio" />

For three years, Feustel worked as a geophysicist for the [[Engineering Seismology Group]], Kingston, Ontario, Canada, installing and operating [[microseism]]ic monitoring equipment in underground mines throughout Eastern Canada and the United States. In 1997, he began working for the Exxon Exploration Company (now [[ExxonMobil]] Exploration Company), [[Houston, Texas]], as an exploration geophysicist designing and providing operational oversight of land, marine, and [[borehole]] [[Reflection seismology#Hydrocarbon exploration|seismic programs]] worldwide.<ref name="nasabio" /> He worked in industry for five years before joining NASA.

== NASA career ==
[[File:Andrew J. Feustel 2007.jpg|thumb|upright|Feustel before training at the [[Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory]] in 2007]]
In July 2000, Feustel was selected as an astronaut candidate by NASA. He reported to the Johnson Space Center in August 2000, where he began NASA's two-year training program, training as a [[Mission Specialist|mission specialist]]. After his initial training, he worked in technical roles the Astronaut Office Space Shuttle and Space Station Branches.<ref name=NASAbio>{{cite web|access-date=March 21, 2018
|url=https://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/biographies/andrew-j-feustel/biography
|title=Andrew J. Feustel (PH.D.) NASA Astronaut|work=Astronaut Biographies|date=March 16, 2016
|publisher=NASA}}</ref>

Feustel's subsequent NASA Astronaut training includes: Field Medical Training, Field Maintenance Training, [[NEEMO|NASA Extreme Environment Mission Operation (NEEMO) X]] in the Aquarius Habitat in Key Largo, Florida; CAVES in Sardinia, Italy; [[National Outdoor Leadership School]] training in Alaska and Mexico; Winter Survival Training with the [[Canadian Armed Forces]]; [[Desert Research and Technology Studies|Desert RATS]] in Arizona; Geotechnical Studies in [[Antarctica]]; and DeepWorker Submersible Pilot Training. He is qualified as a Space Shuttle and Space Station Robotic Arm Operator, [[Flight controller#Spacecraft communicator (CAPCOM)|Capsule Communicator (CAPCOM)]], and Instructor Astronaut for [[Extravehicular activity]] (EVA) training at the [[Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory]].<ref name=NASAbio />

In July 2006, Feustel served as an [[aquanaut]] during the [[NEEMO#NEEMO 10: July 22–28, 2006|NEEMO 10]] mission aboard the [[Aquarius (laboratory)|Aquarius]] [[Underwater habitat|underwater laboratory]], living and working underwater for seven days.<ref name="ten">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/NEEMO/NEEMO10/index.html |title=NASA Uses Undersea Lab to Prep for Future Space Exploration |access-date=September 23, 2011 |publisher=NASA |year=2006 |author=NASA}}</ref> In October 2006, Feustel was announced as a crew member for [[STS-125]], the final Hubble servicing mission by the Space Shuttle. STS-125 launched on May 11, 2009.<ref name="SR1" />

In 2013, Feustel served as cavenaut into the [[ESA CAVES]]<ref>{{Cite journal|date=July 1, 2021|title=Speleology as an analogue to space exploration: The ESA CAVES training programme|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0094576521001478|journal=Acta Astronautica|language=en|volume=184|pages=150–166|doi=10.1016/j.actaastro.2021.04.003|issn=0094-5765|last1=Sauro |first1=Francesco |last2=De Waele |first2=Jo |last3=Payler |first3=Samuel J. |last4=Vattano |first4=Marco |last5=Sauro |first5=Francesco Maria |last6=Turchi |first6=Leonardo |last7=Bessone |first7=Loredana |bibcode=2021AcAau.184..150S |s2cid=234819922 |hdl=11585/819077 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> training in [[Sardinia]], alongside [[Soichi Noguchi]], [[Andreas Mogensen]], [[Nikolai Tikhonov (cosmonaut)|Nikolai Tikhonov]], [[David Saint-Jacques]] and [[Michael Fincke]].

=== STS-125 ===
[[File:Andrew Feustel performs work on the Hubble Space Telescope.jpg|thumb|Feustel in front of the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] during STS-125]]
Feustel's first mission was [[STS-125]], which was successfully launched to repair the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] on May 11, 2009. On this mission, Feustel was a [[mission specialist]], and performed three [[Extra-vehicular activity|spacewalks]] to help repair the telescope itself.<ref name="interview" /> During the mission, Feustel accumulated a total EVA time of twenty hours and thirty eight minutes.<!--<ref name="SR15">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/shuttlemissions/sts125/news/STS-125-01.html |title=STS-125 MCC Status Report #15 |access-date=May 11, 2009 |publisher=NASA |date=May 11, 2009 |author=NASA}}</ref>--> He took with him a copy of "Cosmic Songs" (1878) by the Czech poet [[Jan Neruda]] and [[Emm Gryner]]'s album [[Asianblue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CbP95R9LKzi/ |date=March 18, 2022|access-date=March 18, 2022|title=EMM GRYNER on Instagram: "The astronauts I have met have taught me so much about life on earth. Take @colchrishadfield and @astro_feustel for example. Through Chris...}}</ref>

=== STS-134 ===
[[File:Michael Fincke and Andrew Feustel on the International Space Station.jpg|thumb|right| Feustel (right) pictured with fellow astronaut [[Mike Fincke]] prior to an EVA during STS-134]]
Feustel was a mission specialist on the [[STS-134]] mission, during which he performed three more spacewalks.<ref name="Summary">{{cite web |url=http://www.nasa.gov/pdf/531933main_STS134_missionsummary_5-9-11.pdf |title=STS-134 Mission Summary |author=NASA |date=May 2011 |publisher=NASA |access-date=January 13, 2012}}</ref> During this mission Feustel took a soft toy of the cartoon character [[Mole (Zdeněk Miler character)|Mole]] to space. In July 2011 Feustel and his family flew to [[Czech Republic]] to give that Mole to his creator the Czech animator and illustrator [[Zdeněk Miler]].<ref>{{cite web |publisher=iDNES.cz |url=https://kultura.idnes.cz/zemrel-zdenek-miler-otec-krtecka-ktereho-nam-zavidi-hollywood-p6x-/filmvideo.aspx?c=A111130_175646_filmvideo_jaz |language=cs|title=Pictures of Feustel during the surrender of the soft toy Mole in Czech Republic + article (Zemřel Zdeněk Miler. Otec Krtka, kterého nám závidí Hollywood) |date=November 30, 2011 |access-date=January 25, 2016}}</ref> He was very happy and thanked Feustel with an artwork of him. Just four months later Miler died at the age of 90 years.

=== Expedition 55/56 ===
[[File:ISS-55 EVA-1 (d) Drew Feustel.jpg|thumb| Feustel pictured during an EVA in 2018]]
Feustel returned to space on launching on March 21, 2018<ref name="IndyStar-2018-03-21">{{cite news |last=Siacon |first=Aleanna |date=March 21, 2018 |title=Purdue astronaut Andrew Feustel among NASA crew heading to International Space Station |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/2018/03/21/purdue-astronaut-andrew-feustel-among-nasa-crew-heading-international-space-station/447641002/ |access-date=March 21, 2018 |work=IndyStar}}</ref> for a six month<ref>Interview with Feustel, October 6, 2016.</ref> stay during [[Expedition 55]]/[[Expedition 56|56]]. He served as a flight engineer on Expedition 55, and then became the [[International Space Station]] (ISS) commander of Expedition 56.<ref name="55exp">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-assigns-upcoming-space-station-crew-members |title=NASA Assigns Upcoming Space Station Crew Members |publisher=NASA press release 17-001 |author=Karen Northon |date=January 4, 2017 |access-date=January 21, 2017}}</ref> He returned to Earth on October 4, 2018.

On March 29, 2018, Feustel performed the first EVA of his mission with crewmate [[Ricky Arnold]]. They installed wireless communications equipment on the station's Tranquility module to enhance payload data processing for the [[ECOSTRESS]] experiment (Ecosystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station). They also swapped out high-definition video cameras on the port truss of the station's backbone and removed aging hoses from a cooling component on the station's truss. The duration of the spacewalk was 6 hours and 10 minutes.

=== Deputy Chief of the NASA Astronaut Office ===
Feustel became the Deputy [[Chief of the Astronaut Office|Chief of the NASA Astronaut Office]] in 2020, and served as acting Chief Astronaut starting in November 2022 after [[Reid Wiseman]] stepped down to return as an active duty astronaut. In February, 2023 [[Joseph M. Acaba|Joseph Acaba]] was appointed Chief, with Feustel remaining on as his deputy.

==Post-NASA career==
After working for NASA for 23 years, Drew Feustel announced his retirement from the agency in July 2023.<ref name="nasa20230728">{{Cite web |title=NASA Astronaut Andrew Jay (Drew) Feustel to Leave NASA - NASA |url=https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-astronaut-andrew-jay-drew-feustel-to-leave-nasa/ |date=28 July 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250202090527/https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-astronaut-andrew-jay-drew-feustel-to-leave-nasa/ |archive-date=2 February 2025 |access-date=2025-02-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> In December of that year, [[Vast (company)|Vast]], a space station manufacturer, announced that Feustel would join their team as an advisor.<ref name="vs20231212">{{Cite web |title=Vast Welcomes Veteran NASA Astronaut Dr. Andrew J. Feustel As Its Newest Human Spaceflight Advisor — VAST |url=https://www.vastspace.com/updates/vast-welcomes-veteran-nasa-astronaut-dr-andrew-j-feustel-as-its-newest-human-spaceflight-advisor |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214044406/https://www.vastspace.com/updates/vast-welcomes-veteran-nasa-astronaut-dr-andrew-j-feustel-as-its-newest-human-spaceflight-advisor |date=12 December 2023 |archive-date=14 February 2025 |access-date=2025-02-14 |website=www.vastspace.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Feustel is married to Indira Devi Feustel (née Bhatnagar). Andrew and Indira met as [[undergraduate education|undergraduates]] at the beginning of Indira's master's degree at Purdue University in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]]; they have two sons. He enjoys [[automobile restoration]], [[skiing]] and [[guitar]], and is a member of the astronaut band [[Max Q (Astronaut band)|Max Q]].<ref name="nasabio" />
